extraction.name: C-EVAL
extraction.description: C-EVAL is a comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite designed to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context. It comprises 13,948 multiple-choice questions across four difficulty levels (middle school, high school, college, and professional) and 52 diverse disciplines spanning STEM, social sciences, humanities, and other areas. It includes C-EVAL HARD, a subset of 8 challenging subjects requiring advanced reasoning abilities.
extraction.creator: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He
extraction.citeAs: Huang, Y., Bai, Y., Zhu, Z., Zhang, J., Zhang, J., Su, T., Liu, J., Lv, C., Zhang, Y., Lei, J., Fu, Y., Sun, M., & He, J. (2023). C-EVAL: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models. Thirty-seventh Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems Datasets and Benchmarks Track.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected primarily from mock exams freely available on the internet, past college-level exam questions publicly shared by students from top universities in China, and mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam authorized from the Weipu website. Sourced documents (mostly PDF or Word documents, and some web pages) were parsed automatically or manually into structured formats. Standard subjects for middle school, high school, 25 representative undergraduate subjects, and 12 representative vocational qualifications were included.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Mock exams available on the internet, past exam questions from top universities in China shared by students, and around 2000 mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam authorized from the Weipu website (https://kaoyan.cqvip.com/view/postgraduate/index.aspx).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF documents were converted into text and questions were parsed automatically or manually into a structured format. Questions with fewer than four options were eliminated, and incorrect choices were randomly dropped for questions with more than four options to maintain exactly four choices. Mathematical notations were manually converted to standard LaTeX format. Standard preprocessing pipelines including deduplication, cleaning, and syntax verification for LaTeX notations were applied.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Authors cross-validated and validated the parsed questions over several rounds. For the development set, step-by-step chain-of-thought explanations were generated using GPT-4 prompted with five human-written question-explanation pairs, followed by manual revision by the authors.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Authors of the paper (affiliated with Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tsinghua University, University of Edinburgh, and The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 (used for generating initial step-by-step explanations for the development set)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Development and validation split labels are released publicly, while test split labels are kept private to avoid data leakage and contamination. Model predictions are evaluated via an online submission system maintaining a public leaderboard on https://cevalbenchmark.com.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Aims to foster the development, growth, and comprehensive understanding of foundation models for Chinese users and researchers, analyzing their strengths and shortcomings in a Chinese context.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Analysis of option bias showed minor fluctuations in the proportions of answer choices (A: 22.9%, B: 26.0%, C: 26.4%, D: 24.7%), comparable to MMLU. Geographic biases in existing English benchmarks motivated the creation of this dataset targeting Chinese cultural, historical, and legal knowledge.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: C-EVAL focuses exclusively on multiple-choice questions and does not cover other abilities such as reasoning over and calling APIs, nor dimensions beyond accuracy including safety, bias, and robustness.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and validation of advanced knowledge and reasoning capabilities of large language models/foundation models in zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought settings.
